reasoning_trace.value: The paper discusses integrated sensing and communication in 6G systems, focusing on channel modeling for THz imaging. A 3-D metallic test chart is designed to evaluate the sensing modeling quality. The paper introduces geometrical optics (GO), physical optics (PO), and integral equation (IE) methods for simulating the EM fields and combines them with the EM inverse scattering method for developing the image of the 3-D test chart.

The system mechanism is based on deterministic channel modeling approaches, including GO, PO, and IE methods, to simulate the EM fields of a 3-D test chart. The ISAC coupling mode is achieved through the use of these methods to model the sensing channel.

The paper verifies the physical consistency of the reported metrics by comparing the simulated images obtained using the GO, PO, and IE methods with the measured image obtained through an experimental setup in a chamber. The results show that the IE method agrees well with the measurement, while the GO and PO methods can only show the characteristics of 2-D optical imaging.

The paper identifies the solved problem as the development of a deterministic channel modeling approach for THz imaging in 6G systems. The remaining open challenge is the need for more accurate and efficient channel modeling methodologies that can capture the physical phenomena of real-world 3-D electromagnetic sensing targets.

bibliographic.title: Integrated Sensing and Communication in 6G: The Deterministic Channel Models for THz Imaging
bibliographic.authors: Xianjin Li, Jia He, Ziming Yu, Guangjian Wang, Peiying Zhu

key_contribution.gap_addressed: Need for accurate and efficient channel modeling methodologies for 6G systems
